quotes.text: One of the reasons I want to sit in the chair is 'cause I'm nervous. But the other reason is, I see if she's a secretary, she's gonna sing a song, it might be very funny if she rolls around in a secretarial chair.

And I said, 'Oh, I thought you liked my chair.' And they said, 'No, no, that was good for the audition. But now we're gonna stage it.' And I thought, I really tried hard, but I guess I didn't cut it. I didn't understand [the staging] from a truthful point of view. And Arthur Laurents kept saying to me, 'You're never gonna make it because you're so undisciplined.'
They said to me, 'Oh, do it in your damn chair!' And it stopped the show.

I'm an actress first. Broadway songs tell a story, 'cause they're based on a character. And it's a play for me. It's, how does the character grow? How does she transform from the beginning of the song to the end?

Because it's private, basically. I can just be alone with the music in my headphones. When I sing with headphones, the sound is just - you're enveloped in the orchestra. And then my voice fits into that orchestra, which is much harder to do on stage, because I can't wear those things they wear in the - I don't like anything stuck in my ears. And so you don't get the same kind of sound when you're singing - I can't really hear myself. So it's not as much fun.
